feature_overview.business_goal: Help customers quickly find relevant products through browsing, search, and filtering, increasing product discovery and add-to-cart conversion rate.
scope: Display a paginated grid/list of items
Enable keyword search matching item name and description
Allow filtering by category, price range, and availability
Support sorting by price, newest first, and popularity
Enable item detail view on click
Enable logged-in users to add items to cart or wishlist from listing
Allow admin to mark items as featured
out_of_scope: Detailed item review and rating system
feature_overview.feature_boundary: This Architecture Plan covers only the Item listing page feature and excludes unrelated features.

functional_requirements.description: Any visitor can view a paginated grid/list of items
User can search items by keyword (matches item name and description)
User can filter items by category, price range, and availability (in stock / out of stock)
User can sort items by price (low to high, high to low), newest first, and popularity
User can click an item to view its detail page
User can change the number of items shown per page (e.g., 12/24/48)
Logged-in user can add an item directly to cart or wishlist from the listing page
Admin can mark an item as featured so it appears pinned at the top of the listing

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a keyword search, only items whose name or description contains that keyword are shown
Given a category filter, only items in that category are shown
Given a category filter, only items in that category are shown, and out-of-stock products are still visible but clearly marked as unavailable.
acceptance_criteria.original_description: Given a price range filter, only items within that range are shown

acceptance_criteria.description: Applying multiple filters at once combines them (AND logic, not OR)
Pagination controls correctly reflect total item count and current page
Sorting by price low-to-high always shows the cheapest available item first
The product listing page shall display clear availability indicators for each product, including low-stock warnings and out-of-stock status.
The system shall support inventory reconciliation and provide logs for all stock movements to maintain auditability.

validation_rules.description: Search keywords must match item name or description
Price filters must be numeric and valid ranges
Sorting options must be one of: price_low_to_high, price_high_to_low, newest_first, popularity
Pagination must support 12, 24, or 48 items per page
All product quantity updates must be handled through atomic operations to prevent race conditions during concurrent checkout.
The system shall release expired reservations and prevent unintentional overselling by monitoring reservation timeouts.

non_functional_requirements.description: Listing page must load within 2 seconds for up to 10,000 items
Search/filter results must update within 1 second of applying a filter
Page must be responsive (mobile, tablet, desktop)
Out-of-stock items are still visible but visually de-emphasized and not addable to cart
The system must clearly indicate when an item is out-of-stock but still searchable, using a visual indicator (e.g., strike-through or grayed-out text) and provide an estimated restocking date.
The system shall support efficient search and filtering of products using full-text search, semantic search, and faceted filtering to improve user discovery and conversion rates.
The system shall implement atomic database operations and stock movement logs to ensure accurate inventory tracking and prevent overselling.

architecture_approach.architecture_rationale: Use modular to keep the Item listing page feature separated into presentation, business logic, and data responsibilities where applicable.
architecture_approach.frontend_overview: Frontend design should provide the user-facing entry points, inputs, states, and feedback required by the approved SRS.
architecture_approach.backend_overview: Backend design should process feature requests, enforce business rules, validate inputs, and return structured responses.
architecture_approach.data_overview: Data design should support the data requirements defined in the approved SRS.
architecture_approach.integration_overview: Integration design should follow the API expectations and dependencies listed in the approved SRS.
design_tradeoffs: Design is derived directly from the approved SRS to preserve traceability and feature scope.
Design is kept feature-scoped to preserve feature-by-feature SDLC development.
Internal generation or repair details are kept in backend logs and are not exposed in the approval-ready Architecture Plan.
